html:
The Kussoe were a coastal people of what is now South Carolina, living on the rivers just west of today's Charleston. They were one of the small tribes the English grouped together as the Cusabo, who held the coast from Charleston south to the Savannah River.

They met Spanish soldiers and missionaries from the fort of Santa Elena between the 1560s and 1580s. When the English founded Charles Town in 1670, the Kussoe were among its nearest neighbours. Quarrels over corn and stray livestock led to a short war in 1671, and in the 1670s their leaders ceded land around the Ashley River to the colony. Weakened by disease and by slave raids, including those of the Westo, the Cusabo became "settlement Indians" living among the colonists of Carolina. Most survivors later joined larger nations such as the Yamasee or the Catawba.
